name: Velociraptor
headline: length
subtitle: Estimated adult size
description: Velociraptor was a small, feathered, meat-eating dinosaur that lived in Mongolia and China in the Late Cretaceous, roughly 74 to 70 million years ago. It walked on two legs and had a large sickle-shaped claw on each foot. Museum estimates put it at about 1.8 metres long, far smaller than the animals shown in the Jurassic Park films.

facts.text: The Jurassic Park films showed Velociraptor at about twice its real size, modelled closely on its larger relative Deinonychus.
Velociraptor is now thought to have had a fine covering of feather-like structures.
Velociraptor mongoliensis was named by Osborn in 1924.
Stiffened tendons in its tail helped it keep its balance while striking at prey with one foot raised.

caveats: All sizes are estimates from fossils.
Mass estimates vary a lot: 7 kg (Natural History Museum), 18 kg (AMNH), and 'perhaps no more than 45 kg' (Britannica). The NHM figure is used as the main mass.
The AMNH gives the age as about 80 million years ago; the Natural History Museum gives 74-70 million years ago.
